title: Adaptive intrinsic dimension Mirror allocation
hypothesis: Choosing per-task intrinsic dimension from a shared Mirror orbit, then allocating sparse private residuals only when necessary, improves the quality-bytes frontier over fixed full-dimensional intrinsic task vectors; unrelated tasks should trigger private allocation.
physical_object: frozen random projection U, D=128 to intrinsic d=32, shared across 24 tasks
mirror_coordinate: shared intrinsic vector, per-task Givens angle, per-task active dimension and optional sparse residual
logical_multiplicity: 24 tasks with four intrinsic complexity levels (4, 8, 16, 32)
strata: shared Givens orbit with variable prefix dimensions
independent task vectors with variable prefix dimensions
controls: Mirror orbit with variable active dimension and sparse private fallback
generic PCA with smallest rank meeting 5% training-coordinate error

development.selection_metric: query NRMSE, actual bytes, active dimensions, private values and split events

paid_objects: direct active task coordinates or Mirror shared vector/angles/dimensions
sparse private residual indices int16 and values fp16

success_gate: On aligned variable-rank tasks, adaptive Mirror reaches query NRMSE <=0.05 and improves total serialized quality-bytes over direct adaptive coordinates; independent tasks must be reported as a private-capacity boundary.
failure_gate: Mirror misses aligned quality or provides no total-payload advantage at matched error; generic/adaptive direct controls matching it means no Mirror-specific result.
boundaries: Aligned stratum is teacher-generated from shared Givens orbit
Dimension is inferred from support-fitted coordinates and target tolerance
